svg.title: Who holds the capability
svg.desc: A notebook page with two lanes divided by a dashed vertical boundary labelled the files go out. The left lane, before Nov 4 - Moonshot's side, shows a box for training-data removal (cyber content out of mid-training and RL, general coding kept), a box for the hosted API where the level is Moonshot's to manage, and a note that the 90.5 and 81.0 xdev-bench-hard figures are Moonshot's own on its in-house benchmark, pass@3 over a random subset of runs. One arrow crosses the boundary, labelled Nov 4 - promised, not done, to the right lane, after release - everyone's side, which shows a box for weights on anyone's hardware (everything after belongs to whoever holds the files), a dashed box for fine-tuning that can raise the level again (structural, not an observed test), and a note that the K3.1 Pro license is not published yet and no independent tests exist. A footer states that the numbers are Moonshot's own and the release has not happened.

text.tspan: A capability cut is a starting level, not a ceiling. Release decides who can move it.
